data.title: URL
data.tagline: Describe the exact location of a resource on the web
data.description: A URL contains pieces such as protocol, domain, path, query, and fragment. Together they identify a page or resource and may carry filters or an anchor. Keep public URLs readable and stable, and never place passwords or secrets in them.

use: Carry non-secret search or filter parameters
Jump to a section with a fragment
avoid: Put passwords, tokens, or personal secrets in the URL
Use an unreadable path when a clear one is possible
Treat query parameters as trusted data

lessonPractice.title: Someone wants to send 'unpaid orders, page 3' to a teammate who should open the same result. How should the URL work?

options.label: Keep filters and page number only in memory and share the same /orders URL
options.feedback: In-memory state does not travel with the link, so the teammate opens the default order list.

options.label: Put the filter and page in query parameters and verify that the link reproduces the view
options.feedback: The path identifies the page and query parameters preserve filters and position for another device.

options.label: Put the filters, page number, and login token in the URL and send all of it
options.feedback: Filters may be shareable, but a login token is sensitive and can leak through history, logs, and messages.

data.agentPrompt: Store order filters and page number in URL query parameters so sharing, refresh, and browser Back restore the same result. Never put login tokens or other secrets in the URL. Verify by opening the copied link in a new tab.
